news.title: Databricks 以约 2229 亿美元估值寻求新一轮融资，企业级 AI 投资热潮持续
news.snippet: 美国数据与 AI 公司 Databricks 正寻求新融资，估值约 2229 亿美元，反映企业 AI 投资热情不减。
news.raw_snippet:
Databricks, the U.S. data and artificial intelligence (AI) software company, is negotiating to raise several billion dollars in new funding on the premise of a $225 billion (~300 trillion won) valuation. The Wall Street Journal reported the talks, citing sources familiar with the matter, adding that the discussions are still at an early stage and that both the size of the raise and the final valuation could be adjusted. [...] Founded in 2013, Databricks provides a platform that lets companies consolidate and analyze their internal data and build and run AI applications on top of it. It is one of Silicon Valley's most prominent private companies and is frequently cited as a future IPO candidate. In August, the company said its annualized revenue had surpassed $7 billion (~9.4 trillion won). [...] Market attention is also fixed on how Anthropic trades following its listing. With the debut viewed as a gauge of demand for AI companies, expectations are building for the next wave of IPO candidates. For Databricks, the new funding would give it the firepower it needs to go after the enterprise AI market.

news.title: AI 拟人化——人工智能
news.snippet: AI 拟人化指将人类特质、情感或意图赋予人工智能系统的倾向，对人机交互设计具有重要影响。
news.raw_snippet: AI anthropomorphism is the tendency to attribute human qualities such as emotions, intentions, beliefs, consciousness or moral character to artificial intelligence systems, and the design practice of encouraging that attribution. In AI ethics, it matters because perceived humanness changes how much people trust, disclose to and depend on a system, often beyond what its actual capabilities justify. [...] People humanize AI systems because human social cognition is triggered by surface cues, not by an assessment of what is actually inside the machine. Psychologists describe a default stance in which any agent that produces language or goal-directed behavior is treated as having a mind. This is sometimes called the intentional stance: predicting behavior by assuming beliefs and desires. [...] - Humanlike output is not evidence of experience. Fluent emotional language reflects training data patterns, not demonstrated feelings.
